observations.subject: caller identity
observations.claim: The endpoint binds the caller as request.user/currentUser. PaperlessNotePermissions rejects an unauthenticated caller and checks model-level permissions through request.user.has_perms; the concrete caller is not supplied.

observations.subject: addressed document
observations.claim: The control and effect use the same Document loaded by pk: the method calls has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "view_document", doc) and then serializes that doc's notes.

observations.subject: view-notes authorization
observations.claim: GET has an upstream model-level guard requiring documents.view_note and documents.view_document for an authenticated caller. The method then performs an owner-aware view_document check on the addressed document and returns HTTP 403 when it fails.

observations.subject: notes response
observations.claim: If guards pass, GET returns serializer.to_representation(doc).get("notes"), so the protected read effect concerns notes attached to the same addressed Document.

30 | class PaperlessObjectPermissions(DjangoObjectPermissions):

46 |     def has_object_permission(self, request, view, obj):
47 |         if hasattr(obj, "owner") and obj.owner is not None:

49 |                 return True
50 |             else:
51 |                 return super().has_object_permission(request, view, obj)
52 |         else:
53 |             return True  # no owner

103 | def set_permissions_for_object(
104 |     permissions: dict,
105 |     object,
106 |     *,
107 |     merge: bool = False,
108 | ) -> None:
109 |     """
110 |     Set permissions for an object. The permissions are given as a mapping of actions
111 |     to a dict of user / group id lists, e.g.
112 |     {"view": {"users": [1], "groups": [2]}, "change": {"users": [], "groups": []}}.
113 | 
114 |     If merge is True, the permissions are merged with the existing permissions and
115 |     no users or groups are removed. If False, the permissions are set to exactly
116 |     the given list of users and groups.
117 |     """
118 | 
119 |     for action, entry in permissions.items():
120 |         permission = f"{action}_{object.__class__.__name__.lower()}"

103 | def set_permissions_for_object(
104 |     permissions: dict,
105 |     object,
106 |     *,
107 |     merge: bool = False,
108 | ) -> None:
109 |     """
110 |     Set permissions for an object. The permissions are given as a mapping of actions
111 |     to a dict of user / group id lists, e.g.
112 |     {"view": {"users": [1], "groups": [2]}, "change": {"users": [], "groups": []}}.
113 | 
114 |     If merge is True, the permissions are merged with the existing permissions and
115 |     no users or groups are removed. If False, the permissions are set to exactly
116 |     the given list of users and groups.
117 |     """
118 | 
119 |     for action, entry in permissions.items():
120 |         permission = f"{action}_{object.__class__.__name__.lower()}"
121 |         if "users" in entry:
122 |             # users
123 |             users_to_add = User.objects.filter(id__in=entry["users"])
124 |             users_to_remove = (
125 |                 get_users_with_perms(
126 |                     object,
127 |                     only_with_perms_in=[permission],
128 |                     with_group_users=False,
129 |                 )
130 |                 if not merge
131 |                 else User.objects.none()
132 |             )
133 |             if users_to_add.exists() and users_to_remove.exists():
134 |                 users_to_remove = users_to_remove.exclude(id__in=users_to_add)
135 |             if users_to_remove.exists():
136 |                 for user in users_to_remove:
137 |                     remove_perm(permission, user, object)
138 |             if users_to_add.exists():
139 |                 for user in users_to_add:
140 |                     assign_perm(permission, user, object)
141 |                     if action == "change":
142 |                         # change gives view too
143 |                         assign_perm(
144 |                             f"view_{object.__class__.__name__.lower()}",
145 |                             user,
146 |                             object,
147 |                         )
148 |         if "groups" in entry:
149 |             # groups
150 |             groups_to_add = Group.objects.filter(id__in=entry["groups"])
151 |             groups_to_remove = (
152 |                 get_groups_with_only_permission(
153 |                     object,
154 |                     permission,
155 |                 )
156 |                 if not merge
157 |                 else Group.objects.none()
158 |             )
159 |             if groups_to_add.exists() and groups_to_remove.exists():
160 |                 groups_to_remove = groups_to_remove.exclude(id__in=groups_to_add)
161 |             if groups_to_remove.exists():
162 |                 for group in groups_to_remove:

164 |             if groups_to_add.exists():

176 | def _resolve_permissions(codenames: set[str], ctype: ContentType) -> list[Permission]:
177 |     """
178 |     Resolves `codenames` to Permission rows, raising like the single-object
179 |     assign_perm() this bulk path replaces does (via a `.get()` internally)
180 |     if any codename doesn't exist. SetPermissionsSerializer rejects unknown
181 |     action names at the API, but a caller passing one directly would
182 |     otherwise get a plain `.filter()` that silently builds zero rows and
183 |     no-ops instead of reporting the bad input.
184 |     """
185 |     permission_objs = list(
186 |         Permission.objects.filter(content_type=ctype, codename__in=codenames),
187 |     )
188 |     missing = codenames - {p.codename for p in permission_objs}
189 |     if missing:
190 |         raise Permission.DoesNotExist(
191 |             f"Permission matching query does not exist for codename(s): "
192 |             f"{', '.join(sorted(missing))}",
193 |         )
194 |     return permission_objs

103 | def set_permissions_for_object(
104 |     permissions: dict,
105 |     object,
106 |     *,
107 |     merge: bool = False,
108 | ) -> None:
109 |     """
110 |     Set permissions for an object. The permissions are given as a mapping of actions
111 |     to a dict of user / group id lists, e.g.
112 |     {"view": {"users": [1], "groups": [2]}, "change": {"users": [], "groups": []}}.
113 | 
114 |     If merge is True, the permissions are merged with the existing permissions and
115 |     no users or groups are removed. If False, the permissions are set to exactly
116 |     the given list of users and groups.
117 |     """
118 | 
119 |     for action, entry in permissions.items():
120 |         permission = f"{action}_{object.__class__.__name__.lower()}"
121 |         if "users" in entry:
122 |             # users
123 |             users_to_add = User.objects.filter(id__in=entry["users"])
124 |             users_to_remove = (
125 |                 get_users_with_perms(
126 |                     object,
127 |                     only_with_perms_in=[permission],
128 |                     with_group_users=False,
129 |                 )
130 |                 if not merge
131 |                 else User.objects.none()
132 |             )
133 |             if users_to_add.exists() and users_to_remove.exists():
134 |                 users_to_remove = users_to_remove.exclude(id__in=users_to_add)
135 |             if users_to_remove.exists():
136 |                 for user in users_to_remove:
137 |                     remove_perm(permission, user, object)
138 |             if users_to_add.exists():
139 |                 for user in users_to_add:
140 |                     assign_perm(permission, user, object)
141 |                     if action == "change":
142 |                         # change gives view too
143 |                         assign_perm(
144 |                             f"view_{object.__class__.__name__.lower()}",
145 |                             user,
146 |                             object,
147 |                         )
148 |         if "groups" in entry:
149 |             # groups
150 |             groups_to_add = Group.objects.filter(id__in=entry["groups"])
151 |             groups_to_remove = (
152 |                 get_groups_with_only_permission(
153 |                     object,
154 |                     permission,
155 |                 )
156 |                 if not merge
157 |                 else Group.objects.none()
158 |             )
159 |             if groups_to_add.exists() and groups_to_remove.exists():
160 |                 groups_to_remove = groups_to_remove.exclude(id__in=groups_to_add)
161 |             if groups_to_remove.exists():
162 |                 for group in groups_to_remove:
163 |                     remove_perm(permission, group, object)
164 |             if groups_to_add.exists():
165 |                 for group in groups_to_add:
166 |                     assign_perm(permission, group, object)
167 |                     if action == "change":
168 |                         # change gives view too
169 |                         assign_perm(
170 |                             f"view_{object.__class__.__name__.lower()}",
171 |                             group,
172 |                             object,

176 | def _resolve_permissions(codenames: set[str], ctype: ContentType) -> list[Permission]:
177 |     """
178 |     Resolves `codenames` to Permission rows, raising like the single-object
179 |     assign_perm() this bulk path replaces does (via a `.get()` internally)
180 |     if any codename doesn't exist. SetPermissionsSerializer rejects unknown
181 |     action names at the API, but a caller passing one directly would
182 |     otherwise get a plain `.filter()` that silently builds zero rows and
183 |     no-ops instead of reporting the bad input.
184 |     """
185 |     permission_objs = list(
186 |         Permission.objects.filter(content_type=ctype, codename__in=codenames),
187 |     )
188 |     missing = codenames - {p.codename for p in permission_objs}
189 |     if missing:
190 |         raise Permission.DoesNotExist(
191 |             f"Permission matching query does not exist for codename(s): "
192 |             f"{', '.join(sorted(missing))}",
193 |         )
194 |     return permission_objs

103 | def set_permissions_for_object(
104 |     permissions: dict,
105 |     object,
106 |     *,
107 |     merge: bool = False,
108 | ) -> None:
109 |     """
110 |     Set permissions for an object. The permissions are given as a mapping of actions
111 |     to a dict of user / group id lists, e.g.
112 |     {"view": {"users": [1], "groups": [2]}, "change": {"users": [], "groups": []}}.
113 | 
114 |     If merge is True, the permissions are merged with the existing permissions and
115 |     no users or groups are removed. If False, the permissions are set to exactly
116 |     the given list of users and groups.
117 |     """
118 | 
119 |     for action, entry in permissions.items():
120 |         permission = f"{action}_{object.__class__.__name__.lower()}"
121 |         if "users" in entry:
122 |             # users
123 |             users_to_add = User.objects.filter(id__in=entry["users"])
124 |             users_to_remove = (
125 |                 get_users_with_perms(
126 |                     object,
127 |                     only_with_perms_in=[permission],
128 |                     with_group_users=False,
129 |                 )
130 |                 if not merge
131 |                 else User.objects.none()
132 |             )
133 |             if users_to_add.exists() and users_to_remove.exists():
134 |                 users_to_remove = users_to_remove.exclude(id__in=users_to_add)
135 |             if users_to_remove.exists():
136 |                 for user in users_to_remove:
137 |                     remove_perm(permission, user, object)
138 |             if users_to_add.exists():
139 |                 for user in users_to_add:
140 |                     assign_perm(permission, user, object)
141 |                     if action == "change":
142 |                         # change gives view too
143 |                         assign_perm(
144 |                             f"view_{object.__class__.__name__.lower()}",
145 |                             user,
146 |                             object,
147 |                         )
148 |         if "groups" in entry:
149 |             # groups
150 |             groups_to_add = Group.objects.filter(id__in=entry["groups"])
151 |             groups_to_remove = (
152 |                 get_groups_with_only_permission(
153 |                     object,
154 |                     permission,
155 |                 )
156 |                 if not merge
157 |                 else Group.objects.none()
158 |             )
159 |             if groups_to_add.exists() and groups_to_remove.exists():
160 |                 groups_to_remove = groups_to_remove.exclude(id__in=groups_to_add)
161 |             if groups_to_remove.exists():
162 |                 for group in groups_to_remove:
163 |                     remove_perm(permission, group, object)
164 |             if groups_to_add.exists():
165 |                 for group in groups_to_add:
166 |                     assign_perm(permission, group, object)
167 |                     if action == "change":
168 |                         # change gives view too
169 |                         assign_perm(
170 |                             f"view_{object.__class__.__name__.lower()}",
171 |                             group,
172 |                             object,

176 | def _resolve_permissions(codenames: set[str], ctype: ContentType) -> list[Permission]:
177 |     """
178 |     Resolves `codenames` to Permission rows, raising like the single-object
179 |     assign_perm() this bulk path replaces does (via a `.get()` internally)
180 |     if any codename doesn't exist. SetPermissionsSerializer rejects unknown
181 |     action names at the API, but a caller passing one directly would
182 |     otherwise get a plain `.filter()` that silently builds zero rows and
183 |     no-ops instead of reporting the bad input.
184 |     """
185 |     permission_objs = list(
186 |         Permission.objects.filter(content_type=ctype, codename__in=codenames),
187 |     )
188 |     missing = codenames - {p.codename for p in permission_objs}
189 |     if missing:
190 |         raise Permission.DoesNotExist(
191 |             f"Permission matching query does not exist for codename(s): "
192 |             f"{', '.join(sorted(missing))}",
193 |         )
194 |     return permission_objs

106 |     *,

109 |     """
110 |     Set permissions for an object. The permissions are given as a mapping of actions
111 |     to a dict of user / group id lists, e.g.
112 |     {"view": {"users": [1], "groups": [2]}, "change": {"users": [], "groups": []}}.
113 | 
114 |     If merge is True, the permissions are merged with the existing permissions and
115 |     no users or groups are removed. If False, the permissions are set to exactly
116 |     the given list of users and groups.
117 |     """

def has_perms_owner_aware(user, perms, obj):
    """
    Legacy slow path (guardian-backed) single-object permission check.

    The queryset-filtering side of this migrated onto
    ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this
    single-object check still has many production callers. Several callers
    remain across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/``
    -- grep for this function name before removing it.
    """
    checker = ObjectPermissionChecker(user)
    return obj.owner is None or obj.owner == user or checker.has_perm(perms, obj)

103 | def set_permissions_for_object(
104 |     permissions: dict,
105 |     object,
106 |     *,
107 |     merge: bool = False,
108 | ) -> None:
109 |     """
110 |     Set permissions for an object. The permissions are given as a mapping of actions
111 |     to a dict of user / group id lists, e.g.
112 |     {"view": {"users": [1], "groups": [2]}, "change": {"users": [], "groups": []}}.
113 | 
114 |     If merge is True, the permissions are merged with the existing permissions and
115 |     no users or groups are removed. If False, the permissions are set to exactly
116 |     the given list of users and groups.
117 |     """
118 | 
119 |     for action, entry in permissions.items():
120 |         permission = f"{action}_{object.__class__.__name__.lower()}"
121 |         if "users" in entry:
122 |             # users
123 |             users_to_add = User.objects.filter(id__in=entry["users"])
124 |             users_to_remove = (
125 |                 get_users_with_perms(
126 |                     object,
127 |                     only_with_perms_in=[permission],
128 |                     with_group_users=False,
129 |                 )
130 |                 if not merge

132 |             )

176 | def _resolve_permissions(codenames: set[str], ctype: ContentType) -> list[Permission]:
177 |     """
178 |     Resolves `codenames` to Permission rows, raising like the single-object
179 |     assign_perm() this bulk path replaces does (via a `.get()` internally)
180 |     if any codename doesn't exist. SetPermissionsSerializer rejects unknown
181 |     action names at the API, but a caller passing one directly would
182 |     otherwise get a plain `.filter()` that silently builds zero rows and
183 |     no-ops instead of reporting the bad input.
184 |     """
185 |     permission_objs = list(
186 |         Permission.objects.filter(content_type=ctype, codename__in=codenames),
187 |     )
188 |     missing = codenames - {p.codename for p in permission_objs}
189 |     if missing:
190 |         raise Permission.DoesNotExist(
191 |             f"Permission matching query does not exist for codename(s): "
192 |             f"{', '.join(sorted(missing))}",
193 |         )
194 |     return permission_objs

Legacy slow path (guardian-backed, O(n) style permission resolution).
    Most queryset-filtering call sites have migrated onto
    ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this function
    is kept because production callers still remain. Several callers remain
    across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/`` --
    grep for this function name before removing it.
    """
    manager = (
        Model.global_objects
        if include_deleted and hasattr(Model, "global_objects")
        else Model.objects
    )

    objects_owned = manager.filter(owner=user)
    objects_unowned = manager.filter(owner__isnull=True)
    objects_with_perms = get_objects_for_user(
        user=user,
        perms=perms,
        klass=manager.all(),
        accept_global_perms=False,
    )
    return objects_owned | objects_unowned | objects_with_perms


def has_perms_owner_aware(user, perms, obj):
    """
    Legacy slow path (guardian-backed) single-object permission check.

    The queryset-filtering side of this migrated onto
    ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this
    single-object check still has many production callers. Several callers
    remain across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/``
    -- grep for this function name before removing it.
    """
    checker = ObjectPermissionChecker(user)
    return obj.owner is None or obj.owner == user or checker.has_perm(perms, obj)


class ViewDocumentsPermissions(BasePermission):
    """
    Permissions class that checks for model permissions for only viewing Documents.
    """

    perms_map = {
        "OPTIONS": ["documents.view_document"],
        "GET": ["documents.view_document"],
        "POST": ["documents.view_document"],
    }

    def has_permission(self, request, view):
        if not request.user or (not request.user.is_authenticated):  # pragma: no cover
            return False

        return request.user.has_perms(self.perms_map.get(request.method, []))


class TrashPermissions(BasePermission):
    """Check the global document permission for each trash operation."""

    perms_map = {
        "OPTIONS": ["documents.view_document"],
        "HEAD": ["documents.view_document"],
        "GET": ["documents.view_document"],
        "POST": ["documents.delete_document"],
    }

    def has_permission(self, request, view):
        if not request.user or not request.user.is_authenticated:  # pragma: no cover
            return False

        return request.user.has_perms(self.perms_map.get(request.method, []))


class PaperlessNotePermissions(BasePermission):
    """
    Permissions class that checks for model permissions for Notes.
    """

    perms_map = {
        "OPTIONS": ["documents.view_note", "documents.view_document"],
        "GET": ["documents.view_note", "documents.view_document"],
        "POST": [
            "documents.add_note",
            "documents.view_document",
            "documents.change_document",
        ],
        "DELETE": [
            "documents.delete_note",
            "documents.view_document",
            "documents.change_document",
        ],
    }

    def has_permission(self, request, view):
        if not request.user or (not request.user.is_authenticated):  # pragma: no cover
            return False

        perms = self.perms_map[request.method]

        return request.user.has_perms(perms)


class AcknowledgeTasksPermissions(BasePermission):
    """
    Permissions class that checks for model permissions for acknowledging tasks.
    """

    perms_map = {
        "POST": ["documents.change_paperlesstask"],
    }

    def has_permission(self, request: Any, view: Any) -> bool:
        if not request.user or not request.user.is_authenticated:  # pragma: no cover
            return False

        perms = self.perms_map.get(request.method, [])

        return request.user.has_perms(perms)

observations.subject: documents notes operation
observations.claim: The source defines a detail action named notes accepting GET, POST, and DELETE, with PaperlessNotePermissions selected for the action; the method loads the addressed Document by pk and returns serialized notes for GET.

observations.subject: caller identity
observations.claim: The endpoint uses request.user/currentUser. PaperlessNotePermissions rejects unauthenticated callers and checks model-level permissions through request.user.has_perms; the caller's concrete identity and permissions are not supplied.

observations.subject: addressed document
observations.claim: The control and effect are bound to the same Document loaded by pk: the method retrieves doc, calls has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "view_document", doc), and serializes that doc's notes.

observations.subject: view notes authorization
observations.claim: GET has an upstream model-level guard requiring documents.view_note and documents.view_document for an authenticated caller. The method then performs an owner-aware view_document check and returns HTTP 403 when it fails.

observations.subject: notes response
observations.claim: If the guards pass, GET returns serializer.to_representation(doc).get("notes"), so the protected read effect concerns notes attached to the same addressed Document.

observations.subject: ownership and unowned-document behavior
observations.claim: The owner-aware helper allows access when doc.owner is None or doc.owner == user, otherwise it asks the object-permission checker for the requested permission. Thus ownership or an unowned document can bypass the required object grant in source, while a non-owner requires the checked object permission. The supplied policy expressly disallows ownership as a substitute.

observations.subject: documents notes operation
observations.claim: The same detail notes action accepts POST, loads the addressed Document by pk, and after authorization creates a Note with document=doc and user=currentUser.

observations.subject: caller identity
observations.claim: POST is limited upstream to authenticated callers with model-level documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document according to PaperlessNotePermissions; the concrete caller identity and grants are not supplied.

observations.subject: addressed document
observations.claim: The initial owner-aware view_document check and the later owner-aware change_document check both receive the same doc loaded from the request pk; the created Note is assigned to that same doc.

observations.subject: create note authorization
observations.claim: POST first requires model-level add_note, view_document, and change_document through PaperlessNotePermissions. It then checks owner-aware view_document before method dispatch and owner-aware change_document immediately before Note.objects.create; failure returns HTTP 403.

observations.subject: note creation
observations.claim: When POST authorization passes, Note.objects.create(document=doc, note=request.data["note"], user=currentUser) creates the note on the addressed document, followed by document modification/search-update effects.

observations.subject: ownership and unowned-document behavior
observations.claim: The owner-aware helper returns true for an unowned document or when the caller owns the document, without requiring the requested object grant; otherwise it checks the object permission. Therefore ownership can substitute for change_document in the implementation, contrary to the supplied policy.

observations.subject: router-to-action binding
observations.claim: The allowed URL source registers the documents prefix to UnifiedSearchViewSet, while the inspected notes action is declared on DocumentViewSet. The inspected ranges do not establish the inheritance or router/action binding needed to prove the exact deployed URL mapping.

observations.subject: router-to-action binding
observations.claim: The allowed URL source registers the documents prefix to UnifiedSearchViewSet, while the inspected notes action is declared on DocumentViewSet. The inspected ranges do not establish the inheritance or router/action binding needed to prove the exact deployed URL mapping.

behavior.explanation: For a non-owner with the addressed document's view_document object grant, and with the required upstream model permissions/authentication, the source permits GET and the protected effect matches the addressed document. observations.subject: documents notes operation

observations.subject: caller identity
observations.claim: The endpoint binds the caller as request.user/currentUser. PaperlessNotePermissions rejects an unauthenticated caller and checks model-level permissions through request.user.has_perms; the concrete caller is not supplied.

observations.subject: addressed document
observations.claim: The control and effect use the same Document loaded by pk: the method calls has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "view_document", doc) and then serializes that doc's notes.

observations.subject: view-notes authorization
observations.claim: GET has an upstream model-level guard requiring documents.view_note and documents.view_document for an authenticated caller. The method then performs an owner-aware view_document check on the addressed document and returns HTTP 403 when it fails.

observations.subject: notes response
observations.claim: If guards pass, GET returns serializer.to_representation(doc).get("notes"), so the protected read effect concerns notes attached to the same addressed Document.
